title: Restriction along a monomorphism is surjective on injective modules
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a monomorphism a : U' -> U in a ringed site and an injective module I, the restriction map I(U) -> I(U') is surjective (statement lines 1961-1967). The proof localises the site at U and U' and expresses the restriction map through the functors attached to the monomorphism (proof lines 1969-1992), then extends a section over U' by zero along the monomorphism and applies injectivity of I to produce a preimage (proof lines 1995-2009). The non-formal content is the use of the monomorphism hypothesis to make the extension by zero a subfunctor of the identity, which is what injectivity is applied to. The claim is H2: one adjunction set-up plus one extension argument.
